title: Show the letter grade (A/B/C/D) in the Trade Journal
description: TradeJournalPanel.tsx currently only renders raw grade percentages, with its own code comment explaining the letter grade was deliberately left out pending a documented threshold decision. backend-trade-grade-letter now provides that. Show the new letter grade alongside the existing percentage in TradeJournalPanel's grade cells.

checklist.step: Render the letter grade in GradeCell alongside the existing percentage.
Update/add component tests for the new letter display, covering each letter grade.
Remove or update GradeCell's existing code comment that explained why the letter grade was previously left out, now that it's implemented.

decisions.decision: Render trade_letter_grade appended to the existing percentage text as `${pct}% (${letter})` (e.g. "32.1% (A)"), inside the same Typography span GradeCell already uses for the percentage, rather than a separate Chip/badge element. GradeCell gained a new optional `letterGrade` prop (default null) that only the trade_grade_pct column passes (buy/sell grade columns omit it, since backend-trade-grade-letter deliberately left those percentage-only).
decisions.rationale: A plain parenthetical suffix keeps the letter tightly bound to the exact percentage it was derived from (readers see both together, with the letter as a plain-language gloss on the number) without adding a second visual element, extra spacing, or a new common/ component for a two-character label that only ever appears in this one column. A Chip (as used for exit_reason) was considered and rejected: exit_reason is a categorical tag with no adjacent numeric value to relate it to, which is exactly what makes a separate visual chip earn its place there, whereas here the letter is redundant restated information already implied by the percentage (a reader who knows the A/B/C/D bands from the percentage alone gains nothing structurally different from a chip vs. inline text) -- Elder's own ch. 55 framing treats the letter as a label *for* the percentage, not an independent tag. Also considered showing the letter only via MetricHelp's tooltip text (no visible change to the base cell) -- rejected because the task's own title/checklist explicitly calls for showing the letter 'alongside the existing percentage' in the cell itself, not tucked away in a help popover a user might never open. Kept the letter out of GradeCell's bold/not-bold color logic (isGood still keys off gradePct alone) since that threshold (30%) already exactly coincides with the A/B boundary for trade_grade_pct, so no new visual signal was needed. Buy/sell grade columns don't pass letterGrade at all (defaulting to null, i.e. no parenthetical) rather than being wired to always pass null explicitly, since backend-trade-grade-letter's own decisions record already settled that those two metrics have no letter-grade scale in the book at all.

review.notes: Full review pass: backend pytest --cov=app 99.95% (1139 passed), frontend vitest --coverage 99.72%/99.2%/99.72%/99.79% (all above the 90% gate, no regressions). Static analysis clean: ruff, mypy, eslint, tsc -b --noEmit, and the profit-target wording guard all pass with zero findings. code-review skill (effort medium) against the diff found zero correctness/reuse/simplification issues. No backend/API/schema change in this PR, so no openapi.json regeneration was needed (trade_letter_grade was already added and documented by the already-merged backend-trade-grade-letter task). No new component was introduced (GradeCell already existed in features/portfolio/components/ and only gained an optional prop), so add-frontend-feature's common/-vs-feature placement question doesn't newly arise here. Browser walkthrough: started the app with FINTRADE_DATA_PROVIDER_MODE=fixture, seeded four real closed trades via the actual add/delete-position API (buy/sell prices hand-derived from the fixture provider's own OHLCV + autoenvelope channel to hit each letter band), and drove a real Chromium browser (Playwright, since no browser MCP tool was available in this session) against the running Trade Journal. Confirmed via DOM text/computed styles: Trade Grade column renders '5.0% (D)', '15.0% (C)', '25.0% (B)', '35.0% (A)' -- all four letters -- with the existing >=30% bold threshold still applying correctly (only 35.0% (A) bold). Buy Grade/Sell Grade columns in the same rows render bare percentages ('90.0%', '144.0%', '65.8%', '86.6%', '-61.3%') with no parenthetical letter, confirming those columns are genuinely unaffected, including their own independent >50% bold threshold. No console errors, no failed/4xx+ network requests. Also checked at a 375px viewport: the '(A)' suffix wraps onto its own line inside the Trade Grade cell under narrow width, consistent with how other cells (e.g. entry/exit date+price) already wrap in this table -- not a regression introduced by this change. Ran the persisted e2e suite (make e2e): 18/18 specs passed across dashboard/methodology/navigation/portfolio/stock-analysis/watchlist. The recorded `decisions` entry is sound: it correctly cites Elder ch. 55's letter-as-a-label-for-the-percentage framing, matches backend-trade-grade-letter's own decision that only trade_grade_pct gets a letter (buy/sell have no letter-grade scale in the book), and the rejected Chip/tooltip-only alternatives are reasoned through rather than asserted. Checklist cross-check: all three items are done and none are phrased as 'decide X' needing a further decisions entry beyond the one already recorded. No non-blocking findings were identified in this pass, so no follow-up task was filed for this PR.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend pytest --cov=app (1139 passed, 99.95% coverage) and frontend vitest --coverage (728 passed, 99.72%/99.2%/99.72%/99.79%) -- both match pr-reviewer's reported numbers exactly. Re-ran tsc -b --noEmit and eslint on the two changed files, both clean. Read the full diff: GradeCell's new optional letterGrade prop defaults to null and is only wired into the trade_grade_pct column's render call; buy_grade_pct/sell_grade_pct columns' render calls were left untouched (no letterGrade passed), confirming those columns are genuinely unaffected by inspection, not just by comment. trade_letter_grade already exists on ClosedTradeOut in backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts from the already-merged backend-trade-grade-letter task, so no schema drift. The recorded decisions entry gives a reasoned rationale (parenthetical suffix vs. Chip vs. tooltip-only) consistent with Elder ch.55 framing and backend-trade-grade-letter's own decision. Accept holds.
